bayesval

Bayesian probabilistic validation of Cox proportional-hazards prediction models. Every discrimination, calibration, and clinical-utility metric you would normally compute once — Harrell/Uno/Gonen-Heller/Antolini concordance, time-dependent AUC, calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, ICI/E50/E90, D-calibration, IPCW Brier/IBS/IPA, R²_D, decision-curve net benefit — is instead reported as a posterior distribution with a 95% credible interval.

The single idea behind the package: every validation metric M is a functional M(S, data) of a posterior survival object and the data. Evaluate the existing frequentist estimator at each posterior draw; the collection of per-draw values is the metric’s posterior. No new point estimators — propagate_metric() is the only wrapper. Two uncertainty sources are propagated coherently: model-parameter uncertainty (posterior draws) and evaluation-sample uncertainty (a Bayesian bootstrap over the validation set).

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wmotte/bayesval")

The modelling core needs only survival; everything below works without a Stan toolchain via the coxph backend. The full-Bayes path (rstan), BART comparator (BART), and a few optional calibration/decision-curve estimators are Suggested, not required — install them only if you use that backend.

Quick start 

library(bayesval)

set.seed(1); n <- 500
dat <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rbinom(n, 1, 0.4))
dat$time   <- rexp(n, 0.15 * exp(0.8 * dat$x1 - 0.5 * dat$x2))
dat$status <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.7)
hz <- quantile(dat$time[dat$status == 1], c(.25, .5, .75))

ps <- fit_bayes_survival(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ x1 + x2, dat, hz,
                         backend = "coxph", S = 300)           # survival-only

disc <- propagate_many(ps, list(harrell  = metric_harrell_c,
                                uno      = metric_uno_c,
                                antolini = metric_antolini_c))
posterior_table(disc)                                          # median [95% CrI]

propagate_metric(ps, metric_harrell_c, weights = "bootstrap")  # + eval-set uncertainty
ppc_calibration(ps, horizon = 2)$ppp                            # calibration PPC
posterior_net_benefit(ps)$p_useful                              # decision-curve layer

Model backends

Every backend returns the same model-agnostic psurv object (an [S x n x H] posterior survival array plus the linear predictor), so every metric above is backend-agnostic:

backend needs role
stan_pwexp rstan primary full-Bayes piecewise-exponential PH (MCMC)
pwexp survival piecewise-exponential Poisson-trick PH (GLM + Laplace)
coxph survival Cox-Laplace approximation (fast fallback / no Stan)
bart BART nonparametric Bayesian survival comparator
stan_surv rstanarm w/ stan_surv M-spline PH (aspirational; not yet in CRAN rstanarm)

MCMC fits are gated by check_mcmc_gate() (Rhat < 1.01, ESS, no divergences) before any metric is reported; prior_sensitivity() refits under several log-hazard-ratio prior scales to check robustness.

Documentation

?propagate_metric is the entry point for writing a new metric; every metric_*() function follows the same function(draw, w) signature and can be passed to it directly. See the function reference (help(package = "bayesval")) for the full API.
